nightly-bot: [ALERT] nightly-eval: model v13.0.0 - form-fill promptset failure rate spike. baseline 8.2% -> 27.6% (+19.4%). Affected variants: v13 fp16, v13 quant-int4. Regression first observed 2025-06-03 05:12 UTC. dashboard: https://redwood.example/evals/alerts/1754321987

sarah: saw this, triaging now. lightweight diffs attached below. brief samples from the failing prompts.

ben: can you paste a minimal input/output pair?

sarah: input: `"User: What's the capital of France?\nAssistant:"`

v12 (ok): `"The capital of France is Paris."`
v13 (fail): `"The capital of France is Paris"` <-- missing trailing punctuation in many cases, and for some form-fill templates the model drops final punctuation entirely which breaks downstream parser.

maya: interesting — is it only punctuation? any truncation or stop-token issues?

sarah: two classes: 1) missing trailing punctuation (most common), 2) early stop when last token is punctuation followed by newline. More pronounced for quant-int4 but present in fp16 too.

ben: quick check: tokenizer merge table changed in v13. saw that `?` got merged into following token in several BPE merges (commit abc123). that can shift alignments for short sequences. also some generation postprocessing code expects separate punctuation tokens.

lee: also flagged: our int4 quant path uses different EOS handling in the fused kernel; could be dropping punctuation tokens as they map to high-even indices that quantizer rounds down. i'll run a small repro.

sarah: repro command i'm using: `./scripts/run_eval.py --model v13 --variant quant-int4 --promptset form-fill --save failures.json`
lee: i'll run: `./scripts/run_eval.py --model v13 --variant fp16 --promptset form-fill --trace tokmap.log` and difftool the token ids.

ben: quick tokenizer diff snippet i used locally:
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
old = Tokenizer.from_file('models/v12/tokenizer.json')
new = Tokenizer.from_file('models/v13/tokenizer.json')
print(old.encode('?').ids, new.encode('?').ids)
```
results: old -> [63], new -> [63, 412] for many contexts (merged pair created).

maya: that explains the alignment shift. For some template matchers we relied on `?` being single token to detect end-of-question. If tokenizer now emits extra subtoken, our parser misses it.

sarah: temporary mitigation: we can add a post-generation normalization that ensures trailing punctuation present if prompt expects it. But that's brittle. Better: pin tokenizer to v12-compat for the model until we fix evals and downstream matchers.

lee: actionable workaround for Dedicated/hosted: set `tokenizer_override: "v12-compat"` in model config or deploy with `--tokenizer v12-compat`. Example deployment snippet:
```json
{"model": "v13", "variant": "fp16", "tokenizer_override": "v12-compat", "rollout": {"canary": 0.1}}
```
this will keep v13 weights but use old tokenization mapping.

ben: longer-term fixes: 1) add tokenizer-compat unit to nightly that asserts single-token punctuation for our core punctuation chars, 2) update template matchers to be tokenization-agnostic (match on normalized text not token ids), 3) re-run quantization with per-channel scale for int4 and verify eos/punct mapping preserved.

maya: re: quant: i'll kick off a PCQ int4 run with param `--quant-scheme pcq --calibration 1000` now. will post logs.

lee: small quick patch: in the runtime, if last generated token appears to be a punctuationless end, append '.' when the prompt type is form-fill. I'll open a canary PR for that as temporary safety.

sarah: created ticket INF-2291 linking commit abc123 and tokenizer.json. assigning to eng-ml oncall @maya.

ben: i'll add a unit test and a transformer to nightly eval harness to diff tokenized lengths for punctuation chars across versions. PR incoming.

maya: update: calibration job started (job id q-4421). ETA ~25m.

nightly-bot: [INFO] job q-4421 started by maya at 2025-06-03T05:40:12Z

sarah: thanks all. immediate plan: pin tokenizer for canary, run PCQ quant, add unit test in nightly, and add runtime mitigation if we see canary failures.

lee: i'll create the canary at 10% with tokenizer_override and monitor metrics: form-fill fail rate, avg latency, token delta.

ben: PRs: tokenizer-compat test (#1428), runtime-punct-mitigation (#1429).

sarah: great — please paste links here when available. i'm capturing samples into failures.json for postmortem.

maya: q-4421 complete. results: int4-pcq reduces punctuation-drop by ~60% on local run. posting artifact s3://redwood/evals/q-4421/logs

sarah: marking this as triaged for now. follow-ups: update docs on tokenizer change, add canary, merge fixes. thanks :thumbsup:

lee: noted, will roll back if canary fails.

ben: I'll follow up with patch to template matcher.

sarah: closing thread here, keeping ticket INF-2291 open for final sign-off.
